answer: Each new agent must lock a ferrous collateral bond for several epochs before its attestations count. Bonds collect in a shared lagoon of pending and slashed stakes; a tight clique of mutually attesting newcomers has its bonds burned. Establishment also requires countersignatures from peers on a different graph knoll—a separate high-degree region of the attestation landscape—so cloning one cluster cannot mint a majority. An attacker thus funds a fresh bond and must earn independent peer coverage for every forged identity, a cost that scales linearly with sybil count.
